---
title: "Fuel Economy & EV Range"
subtitle: "How recent gas, hybrid, and electric vehicles compare on efficiency, range, and yearly energy cost"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

recent_df <- read_csv("data/processed/recent_vehicles_2022_2027.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

mpg_df <- recent_df |> filter(!is.na(mpg_city), !is.na(mpg_highway), !is.na(powertrain))
n_mpg <- nrow(mpg_df)

ev_df <- recent_df |>
  filter(powertrain == "Electric", !is.na(electric_range), electric_range > 0)

cost_df <- recent_df |> filter(!is.na(annual_fuel_cost), !is.na(powertrain))
n_cost <- nrow(cost_df)
```

Today's car shoppers choose between traditional fuel engines, hybrids, and pure battery-electric vehicles. Looking across recent 2022–2027 models, we compare how each powertrain handles city traffic versus open-highway cruising, which electric brands travel farthest on a single charge, and how much drivers actually spend on fuel or electricity each year.

## City Traffic vs. Highway Cruising

::: {.plot-container}
```{r}
#| label: fig-city-hwy-mpg
#| echo: false

mpg_plot_df <- mpg_df |>
  mutate(
    unit_label = if_else(powertrain == "Electric", "MPGe", "MPG"),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", year, " ", make, " ", model, "</b><br>",
      "Trim: ", trim, "<br>",
      "Powertrain: ", powertrain, " (", body_group, ")<br>",
      "City: ", mpg_city, " ", unit_label,
      " | Highway: ", mpg_highway, " ", unit_label
    )
  )

p_city_hwy <- ggplot(
  mpg_plot_df,
  aes(x = mpg_city, y = mpg_highway, color = powertrain, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#666666",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Electric" = "#d90429",
    "Hybrid" = "#ef233c",
    "Plug-in Hybrid" = "#ff758f",
    "Gas" = "#111111",
    "Diesel" = "#7a7a7a"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "City vs. Highway Efficiency Across Powertrains (N = ",
      comma(n_mpg), " Recent Trims)"
    ),
    x = "City Efficiency (MPG / MPGe)",
    y = "Highway Efficiency (MPG / MPGe)",
    color = "Powertrain"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p_city_hwy, tooltip = "text", height = 450) |>
  layout(
    autosize = TRUE,
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    margin = list(t = 45, r = 20, b = 75, l = 65)
  ) |>
  config(responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

Gasoline and diesel cars sit above the dashed diagonal line because their engines run more efficiently at steady highway speeds than in stop-and-go traffic. Electric vehicles flip that pattern completely, sitting below the line because regenerative braking recaptures energy every time the driver slows down in the city while wind resistance works hardest on the highway. Conventional hybrids bridge the middle, delivering nearly even efficiency everywhere.

## Single-Charge Range Across Electric Brands

::: {.plot-container}
```{r}
#| label: fig-ev-range-mfr

ev_mfr <- ev_df |>
  summarize(
    n_trims = n(),
    mean_range = mean(electric_range),
    max_range = max(electric_range),
    mean_mpge = mean(mpg_combined, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cost = mean(annual_fuel_cost, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = make
  ) |>
  filter(n_trims >= 10) |>
  mutate(
    make = fct_reorder(make, mean_range),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", make, "</b> (n = ", n_trims, " EV trims)<br>",
      "Average Range: ", round(mean_range, 0), " miles<br>",
      "Longest-Range Trim: ", round(max_range, 0), " miles<br>",
      "Average Efficiency: ", round(mean_mpge, 0), " MPGe<br>",
      "Avg Annual Electricity Cost: ", dollar(round(mean_cost, 0))
    )
  )

n_ev_mfr_trims <- sum(ev_mfr$n_trims)

p_ev_range <- ggplot(
  ev_mfr,
  aes(x = mean_range, y = make, fill = mean_mpge, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " mi")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#202020", high = "#ef233c") +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "Average Single-Charge Driving Range by EV Brand (N = ",
      comma(n_ev_mfr_trims), " Battery-Electric Trims)"
    ),
    x = "Average EPA Electric Range (Miles)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Avg MPGe"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggplotly(p_ev_range, tooltip = "text", height = 520) |>
  layout(
    autosize = TRUE,
    margin = list(t = 45, r = 20, b = 50, l = 95)
  ) |>
  config(responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

Focusing strictly on pure battery-electric cars reveals two very different engineering paths to long driving range. Sleek sedan specialists like Lucid and Tesla pair long driving distances with bright-red high efficiency through low weight and smooth aerodynamics, whereas electric truck makers like Chevrolet, Rivian, and GMC reach long range by fitting huge, heavy battery packs that draw noticeably more electricity per mile.

## Yearly Fuel and Electricity Costs

::: {.plot-container}
```{r}
#| label: fig-annual-fuel-cost

cost_summary <- cost_df |>
  summarize(
    n_trims = n(),
    mean_cost = mean(annual_fuel_cost),
    median_cost = median(annual_fuel_cost),
    .by = powertrain
  ) |>
  mutate(
    powertrain = fct_reorder(powertrain, mean_cost),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", powertrain, "</b> (n = ", comma(n_trims), " trims)<br>",
      "Average Annual Cost: ", dollar(round(mean_cost, 0)), "/yr<br>",
      "Typical (Median) Cost: ", dollar(round(median_cost, 0)), "/yr"
    )
  )

p_cost <- ggplot(
  cost_summary,
  aes(x = mean_cost, y = powertrain, fill = powertrain, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_dollar(suffix = "/yr")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Electric" = "#d90429",
    "Hybrid" = "#ef233c",
    "Plug-in Hybrid" = "#ff758f",
    "Gas" = "#202020",
    "Diesel" = "#666666"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "Average Estimated Yearly Energy Cost by Powertrain (N = ",
      comma(n_cost), " Recent Trims)"
    ),
    x = "Estimated Annual Fuel or Electricity Cost",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p_cost, tooltip = "text", height = 360) |>
  layout(
    autosize = TRUE,
    margin = list(t = 45, r = 20, b = 45, l = 95)
  ) |>
  config(responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

Those efficiency gains show up directly in owners' wallets. Pure electric vehicles cost roughly a quarter as much to power each year as traditional gasoline or diesel models, saving typical drivers thousands of dollars over several years of ownership, while hybrids offer meaningful yearly pump savings for drivers without home charging.
